SYN-D01-C01-DIAGNOSIS.finding: COVID-OUT reported a lower hazard of clinician-diagnosed Long COVID, with interpretation limited by an indexed correction. ACTIV-6’s secondary diagnosis estimate favored metformin but its interval included no difference.
SYN-D01-C01-DIAGNOSIS.magnitude: COVID-OUT: reported hazard ratio 0.59 (95% CI 0.39–0.89), subject to the correction notice. ACTIV-6: risk difference −0.7 percentage points (95% credible interval −1.5 to 0.1).
limits: COVID-OUT enrolled adults with overweight or obesity and no known prior infection; ACTIV-6 allowed prior infection and vaccination.
The COVID-OUT report has an indexed correction and conflicting cumulative-incidence values, making its absolute risk reduction uncertain.
The ACTIV-6 diagnosis endpoint was secondary, and its interval was not adjusted for multiple comparisons.

SYN-D01-C01-RECOVERY.magnitude: Recovered at eight weeks: 84/132 (63.6%) with metformin versus 90/132 (68.2%) with placebo.
limits: The trial abstract notes limited applicability to more severe or persistent Long COVID.
The trial did not establish equivalence between treatment and placebo.

SYN-D03-C01-SEVERITY.magnitude: The primary symptom-severity comparison was not statistically significant.
limits: The small, single-center trial closed early after its futility criterion was reached.
The primary symptom-severity outcome combines six symptoms; the separate fatigue result answers a narrower question.
Lower fatigue scores are better; the positive point estimate does not favor active treatment.
Fatigue was a secondary outcome in a trial with several symptom measures.

SYN-D03-C01-PHENOTYPES.magnitude: No significant primary benefit was reported for the studied symptom phenotypes.
limits: Different phenotypes used different primary outcomes.
The findings apply to the selected symptom groups and tested treatment duration.

SYN-D01-C25-EXPLORATORY.finding: An exploratory companion analysis linked metabolic and brain-connectivity changes with cognitive scores in the metformin schizophrenia trial.
SYN-D01-C25-EXPLORATORY.magnitude: Blood analyses involved 58 participants and MRI analyses 33, from the 72-person parent trial. These subgroup counts describe the mechanistic sample.
limits: Unadjusted exploratory tests, missing samples and potential confounding limit interpretation.
This is a companion analysis of the cognitive trial, not an independent replication.

SYN-D01-C30-BACKGROUND.magnitude: The review summarizes walking speed, strength and exercise responses across different studies.
SYN-D01-C30-BACKGROUND.evidenceBase: A 2023 narrative review of metformin and physical function.
limits: Few included trials specifically recruited people with sarcopenia, and exercise trials tested metformin alongside training.
The review predates the 2025 MET-PREVENT trial.

SYN-D13-C29-NBUVB-BACKGROUND.finding: The textbook describes a small atorvastatin trial as finding no additional repigmentation or disease-stabilization benefit when added to narrowband UVB.
SYN-D13-C29-NBUVB-BACKGROUND.magnitude: A secondary account of a 30-person trial.
SYN-D13-C29-NBUVB-BACKGROUND.evidenceBase: A textbook account of a randomized single-blind trial.
limits: This row represents the textbook account; the original trial is the primary source for methods and adverse effects.

SYN-D07-C18-BACKGROUND.magnitude: A narrative account of earlier investigations, rather than a separate treatment-effect estimate.
limits: The textbook is a secondary source; clinical findings and laboratory experiments require separate interpretation.
